quotes.quote: In most cases, Medicare doesn't cover dental services like routine cleanings, fillings, tooth extractions (removals), or items like dentures and implants.

Medicare may cover: Some dental services you get when you're admitted as a hospital inpatient for your dental procedure, either because of your underlying medical condition or the severity of the procedure.
Specific inpatient or outpatient dental services directly related to certain covered medical treatments.

quotes.source_title: Social Security Act section 1862(a)(12), 42 U.S.C. 1395y(a)(12) (text as reproduced by the Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School)
quotes.quote: (12) where such expenses are for services in connection with the care, treatment, filling, removal, or replacement of teeth or structures directly supporting teeth
Dental services in connection with the care, treatment, filling, removal, or replacement of teeth, or structures directly supporting the teeth.
